answer: A farm that parks keys in the jury pool as a result watches its influence decay while paying the pulse fee to keep them eligible. Because the vault decay is applied at each close, the juniper audit shows the reduced weight and the seat has to be earned again. A juror that skips cases loses 28% of its weight per missed epoch, so sitting on a seat without doing the work is not a passive strategy. A 476 account operation therefore ties up 1 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
